name: Nintendo Switch Pro Controller
notes: 170-byte BLUETOOTH descriptor, extracted byte-exact from a live Pro Controller's SDP cache (issue #37, 2026-07-22): report 0x3F is a real HID gamepad (16 buttons, null-state hat, X/Y/Rx/Ry 16-bit), the full-mode family 0x21/0x30 (48-byte) and 0x31-0x33 (361-byte) are vendor blobs, outputs 0x01/0x10/0x11/0x12 (48-byte). DirectInput parses only 0x3F, so full-mode streaming is invisible to joy.cpl, matching real Bluetooth hardware in every state. nativeDescriptor preserves the 203-byte USB descriptor (DJm00n/ControllersInfo) the profile shipped through v1.3.20; the earlier note claiming USB and BT share a descriptor was wrong. connection=bluetooth + versionNumber=0 match the live pad's presentation (HidD attributes version 0x0000, SDL hidapi bus BLUETOOTH via BTHENUM compat IDs), which SDL requires: HIDAPI_DriverSwitch on a non-BT bus demands the 0x80 USB handshake this descriptor does not carry.
